recipes.name: A Baker's Secret for Bread Machines
ingredients_raw: 7 fluid ounces warm water (110 degrees F/45 degrees C)

steps.text: Ignore the bread machine directions. Place warm water and lard into the bread machine pan. Sprinkle in the yeast. Pour in flour and salt. Toss in cinnamon if desired. Select cycle; press Start.

raw_recipe.headline: A Baker's Secret for Bread Machines
raw_recipe.description: Ignore your bread machine instructions for this basic white bread made with lard and an optional bit of cinnamon. Instead, layer the ingredients in the prescribed manner and you are good to go.

review.reviewBody: It's a keeper, BUT with a few alterations. I did it first exactly has laid out, and it was too salty and didn't rise. The second time, I put the yeast in in the traditional way, on top. I also halved the salt, added one tablespoon of honey, and substituted butter for the lard. It turned out great this way!! And I never like homemade bread!

I had printed this recipe off in 2010 (!) and just made it a few days ago! In 2010 it was called "A Baker's Secret for Bread Machines." I'm on my 2nd bread machine--had a West Bend for 20+ years that I used 1-2 times weekly before it finally bit the dust. I then got a Cuisinart about 3 years ago--don't like it as well as it's a little more temperamental and I've sometimes had loaves that simply haven't turned out. 

I made this recipe as written--didn't add the optional cinnamon. When I added the flour, I didn't smooth it over. When it was done baking, I was surprised to see that the loaf hadn't risen much and the top was kind of misshapen, apparently because I hadn't leveled the flour off after adding it. Therefore, I expected the loaf to be uncooked in the middle or have some other issue rendering it unedible. It was done. It's a dense bread but I think it's supposed to be that way--I don't think it's any fault of my machine. It did have a nice crust--reminiscent of "artisan" breads. I eagerly sliced it and put butter on it. Taste was very disappointing--there was NO flavor to this bread! The next time I had some, I toasted it, thinking that might improve it. Nope. I love bread and usually will gobble up a homemade loaf in a few days. Haven't eaten any more of this bread for the last 4-5 days . Given how tasteless it is, I might cut it into cubes and make croutons out of it. Others have commented that the bread needs sugar for the yeast.

LOVE it! After reading some of the other reviews, I used 2 T olive oil and 1 t sugar. I put the water, sugar, olive oil and yeast in the bottom of the pan and left proof for 10 minutes before adding the rest of the ingredients. It turned out so nice and fluffy/light. Didn't fall or anything. Defintely a keeper! :)

After reading reviews and because I wanted sweet bread, I used 8oz of warm water, 2 tbsp margarine, 2 tbsp vegetable shortening, and half a cup of sugar and a tbsp of honey. Everything else I kept the same and I put it on dough cycle and made beautiful dinner rolls.

I loved this bread! Substitued olive oil for the lard, and added 1 teaspoon sugar to the mix. Placed a little of the warm water, the sugar and yeast in the bottom of the machine bowl and left to proove for ten minutes before addding the rest of the ingredients. Then baked on fast cycle (or near 2 hour cycle) and light crust selection.

Just because there are 40 years of master baking, doesn't mean you can run a bread machine. 

I followed the instructions, but varied the ingredients a bit. Someone said that theirs didn't rise because there was no sugar to feed the yeast, so I added 1T of sugar, substituted butter for the lard, and followed the rest. What I got was a lumpy mass of something that resembled bread, but was tough and salty, even with the added sugar! I couldn't taste the cinnamon at all.

I'm trying it again, following the suggestion of cutting the salt in half, and using 1T of honey instead of sugar, and putting the yeast on top of the other ingredients. Toward the end of the kneading cycle I noticed it was several balls of yucky and not all of the flour was incorporated, so I added more water, approx. 1/3C. After adding the water, it looks like a ball of dough, so here's to hoping it rises and survives the punch down. If it tastes good, I'll be making it again, otherwise, I'm looking for a different recipe.

Like many, I subbed margarine for the lard, put the yeast on top and added a tablespoon of sugar - and this bread is the best that's come out of my bread machine yet! The crust was actually edible instead of a near-steel casing, and the bread was light and soft instead of almost-gooey. This will definitely be made more often at my house!

I've been looking for a great all-purpose bread. I read other reviews and followed the advice to add a little sugar. I used olive oil in place of the lard/butter and I added 1 tsp. dill, 1/4 tsp pepper and cut the salt in half. We'll see if it turns out! I'll follow up on this review once it's done!

Update: a little blah... next time I will try it with butter and add more dill.

I used shortening due to not having any lard, and 1/3 cup of honey. I also use half bread flour, the other half whole wheat. This recipe is great! I have tried so many recipes to use for my bread machine and the bread has come out horrible. This recipe is the one I will always use because I finally am making what I wanted!

Im so happy that I found this recipe! Excellent! I followed some advice and added olive oil instead of lard and added 2 tbsps sugar for some added sweetness. I also didnt have bread flour but it turned out great with unbleached all purpose flour. Turned out yummy!! Definitely a keeper!

Finally, a recipe that makes the best buns next to a boxed mix. Added 1T sugar and dry milk powder, also mixed the white flour with whole-grain, and perfect buns again. Thank you. Trust me, I've tried them all.

Would be zero stars if I could. This was a complete disaster. Not enough liquid to even make something that even resembled dough. I dumped it all out after less than an hour. Not going yo waste electricity on this mess.
My recipe has been changed so much it is unrecognizable! Look for the never-fail white at "Professional Bread Machine - White"
gooey mess after measuring the ingredients exactly.
This didn't turn out at all. I did it exactly as said in the recipe, and I got a small, hard, weirdly shaped loaf. Definitely won't be making this again.
I used this dough recipe to make cinnamon rolls, came out awesome!
It tastes bland. Kids did not like it at all.

I followed the recipe but found the bread very bland. The bread did not rise as high as many of the others I've made, but it is very simple & quick to make.
 I think I will use what's left for toasted bread crumbs, it should be fine for that.
Nope, this is not THE recipe for us....sorry. I have been doing bread machine bread for years and this one? Not so much. Sorry :-(
So true
